By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Two South African Nuclear activists took on the state with limited resources and one a resounding victory that could change the course of our history

Unique Selling Point:
International recognition for two nuclear activists

Summary:
When South Africa's Joemat Peterson signed a nuclear deal with Russia for 9600 MW of power in a secret deal that could later bankrupt the country, two tiny underfunded NGO's decided to take on the fight. This month they will receive international recognition from the worlds most prestigious environmental prize.
Carte goes back to look at how this David and Goliath battle was fought and won

Further information:
In its papers, Earthlife Africa Jhb and SAFCEI maintained that the
minister has failed to put the necessary processes in place to ensure
that the nuclear procurement deal is conducted lawfully and meets the
requirements of the constitution for a fair, equitable, transparent,
competitive and costs effective process:
"Notwithstanding the vast sums of money to be committed, and the
potentially long-term effect on the economy and for consumers of
electricity and present and future generations of South Africans, the
decision to proceed with procuring these nuclear power plants (the so
called nuclear fleet), and to have concluded such procurement in the
next few months, has occurred without any of the necessary statutory and
constitutional decisions having been lawfully taken"Senior Programme Officer at Earthlife Africa Jhb. Makoma Lekalakala
states: "Government's ongoing efforts to procure 9600 MW of nuclear
energy behind closed doors and without taking the public into its
confidence marks a critical point in the post 1994 political landscape.
Civil society's attempts to obtain information on and answers to serious
public interest questions regarding the potential negative impacts (such
as impacts on electricity prices) of the procurement deal of the century
have been frustrated and blocked at every turn. Lekalakala explains that
this court case is not about the fact that nuclear energy is
environmentally destructive and a false solution to the current
electricity crisis, but is about lawful, constitutional, open and
responsive governance. In a context of ongoing secrecy by government,
the publics' right to participate in decisions that have far- reaching
implications for both current and future generations of South Africans
needs to be respected and protected . "We are concerned citizens
standing up against the unlawful and unconstitutional exercise of power
by government, and in the public interest are going to court in an
effort to protect our constitutional rights".
At a board meeting in October 2014, SAFCEI elected to seek legal counsel
to investigate the nuclear contracts which South Africa had signed.
Faith communities are gravely concerned at the government's continued
support for nuclear energy despite a lack of evidence that South Africa
can afford it.
SAFCEI believes that this new nuclear power poses unacceptable
environmental, social and economic risks to the people of South Africa
and believes that concentrated focus on renewable energy is the key to
alleviating poverty and addressing the developmental needs of the
country.
"Ethical governance has to be the cornerstone of true democracy", stated
Liziwe McDaid, spokesperson for SAFCEI, "this new democracy must be
protected from people in positions of power who act without regard to
proper process, without accountability and risk bankrupting the
country". McDaid added that: "Faith demands courage. As people of
faith, we are concerned about the direction in which we are currently
being led by our leadership. We request transparency, honesty and
openness around the decisions being made for our future."
The Russian nuclear agreement contains specific clauses that could have
potentially devastating consequences for South Africa. These include
that South Africa will be liable for any environmental including
radioactive accidents and any resultant economic consequences, while
Russia will not have any liability. It also states that South Africa
cannot procure nuclear services from any other entity without the
consentof Russia.
SAFCEI board member and Buddist Ani Tsondru comments that:
"In effect, this could result in massive economic and social impacts for
South Africans. We will be in debt to the Russians nuclearcorporation,
and potentially suffering from a dual burden of insufficient funds to
build hosptials, houses and schools, while having to foot the bill for
environmental clean-up costs if there is an accident. This is a gross
injustice to the people of South Africa and must be stopped".
The court application therefore seeks to set aside the framework
agreements

Press Release:


Goldman Girls
The new nuclear deal pushed by former President Jacob Zuma would have been the largest procurement ever undertaken in South Africa. It was supposed to be transparent and affordable, but it was neither, as the Department of Energy drove the process in secret. But two small NGOs, Earthlife Africa and SAFCEI refused to accept that the trillion rand procurement was a done deal. Leading their campaign, were two activists forged in the struggle, Makoma Lekalakala and Liziwe Mcdaid. This week they received the international Goldman prize for stopping the State’s nuclear procurement in its tracks.


Script:


GOLDMAN GIRLS SCRIPT FINAL SCRIPT TX 29th April 2018

Commentary One
In 2014, the nuclear deal, driven by the former president himself, seemed unstoppable. Six to 8 reactors supplying 9600 MW of power were coming our way, and if you joined the dots the Russian state owned nuclear company Rosatom was clearly a front runner

Up sound Putin and Zuma

Commentary two
This would be the largest procurement ever undertaken in South Africa. It was supposed to be transparent and affordable, but it was neither, as officials in the department of energy drove the process in secret

Zizamele Mlambo: The preparatory work is at an advanced stage and the country is ready to roll out the programme

Up sound protest

Commentary Three
But two small NGO's refused to accept we were about to spend a trillion rand, potentially bankrupting future South Africans, without any public participation.

Liz:
The public they didn't seem to appear on the radar! The whole process continued as if there was no constitutional issue

Commentary Four
SAFCEI is a small faith- based NGO. Liz Mcdaid its eco justice leader

Liz
I think the government kept saying we are going to follow due process while behind the scenes they were doing the exact opposite.

Commentary Five
SAFCEI joined forces with Earthlife Africa. Director, Makoma Lekalakala, like Liz was forged in the struggle. Together, these women, would soon become a spoke in the wheel of the state machinery

Devi
Were you always a warrior, somebody who spoke up and said what you felt
Makoma
That is me
Devi
You upset a lot of people
Makoma
I did I know. THAT I Know!

LINK
They had been working quietly behind the scenes, but when then minister of Energy, Tina Joemat Peterson signed the Russian Intergovernmental agreement, they knew it was time to act

Makoma
If I call myself a citizen of this country I have a responsibility to ensure that whatever happens - particularly that our democratic ideals that we fought for, flourish. If I didn't do that I would be complicit of something that was not supposed to happen

Commentary six
The intergovernmental agreement with Russia was signed with the authority of former President Zuma. Four weeks before it was signed, he visited President Putin in Russia. Shortly after the signing, the Voice of Russia released this statement

Up sound

"South Africa's Nuclear Procurement Project is estimated at 40 billion dollars to 50 billion dollars. Eight power generating units with more than one GigaWatt of power capacity each are due to be built under the project….

…Russia and South Africa have already reached agreement to that end"

Commentary six A
But that inconvenient announcement was soon denied by South Africa, as journalists clambered for answers

Liz
We hear we have signed an agreement. Have we? Yes, we have, oh no sorry we haven't, not really. Have we? haven't we? And what exactly did we sign? No real answers

Commentary seven
The answers came from this Russian antinuclear activist, Vladimir Slovyak who leaked the agreement to Earthlife Africa. In it all liability for nuclear accidents had been assigned to South Africa

Liz:
for me the biggest thing was that if something goes wrong the Russians would walk away so on what basis are you giving them any incentive to do a good job?

Makoma Lekalakala
That is what our government had signed with Russia - actually putting the lives of SA at risk Devi
Is that normal? I build it, if it doesn't work out, sorry for you
Makoma
That tells us these are corrupt deals - if there are corrupt deals there will be disregard for environment and disregard for people

Liz Mcdaid
How can you put that into a contract? It's just totally irresponsible

Commentary eight
And so, they fought back - first on the streets, then outside parliament when the cabinet had its meetings

Up sound

They mobilized in townships, in the cities.

Up sound

They started fundraising when it became clear the only way to stop the nuclear juggernaut, was to go to court.

Liz
it was a case of saying we are never going to give up. We can't just let bullies get away with it, and you just have to keep going. GOOD MUST TRIUMPH!

Commentary nine
For over two years, Liz and Makoma were on the front lines. The Legal resources centre and attorney Adrian Pole played a pivotal role preparing their court papers. In 2015, finally they were ready to file

Makoma
There are people who said we are crazy! When we announced publicly that we are filing a case against the president, the speaker, the Department of energy. There are people who would say are you sure of what you are doing?

Commentary ten
They argued that the procurement was unlawful and secretive, that former President Zuma, Minister Joemat Peterson, and NERSA had violated the constitution, parliament had been circumvented and there had been no public participation

Liz
They took this as a case they would easily win, …if the government underestimated our team, maybe they arrogantly thought the law didn't count anymore they could carry on regardless

Commentary Eleven
Time was against them, as the state and its agencies, drove the process forward with little regard for their court proceedings. In 2015 NECSA CEO Pumzile Tshelane, was optimistic we could easily build the reactors within 8 years

Phumzile Tshelane
The normal construction period for reactors is five years and now we have eight years to go. We certainly can fit a 60-month period between now and 2023- its tight but its achievable.

Commentary twelve
The court date was set for December 2016. The state argued that these anti-nuclear lobbyists were trying to derail the nuclear plans by turning speculation into facts. They also argued that a South African court had no jurisdiction over intergovernmental agreements

Liz
Yes, that was an international agreement so when we enter into international agreements we have no say, like hey? how does that work?

LINK
By December 2016 they were all exhausted, but the state still had some dirty tricks up its sleeve

Liz
they were being taken to court for a document that had been signed in secret and they arrived with another document that was even more secret and claimed because they had this second document the whole court case was now moot

Commentary thirteen
Their case was postponed till Feb 2017. Meanwhile as former President Zuma pushed hard for nuclear his own finance minister pushed back.

Zuma
I have decided to make changes to the national executive

In a late-night cabinet reshuffle at the end of March 2017 the former president fired his finance and energy minister. Perhaps the nuclear deal was taking too long

But only weeks later, on the eve of Freedom Day, the former president's nuclear plans would come crashing down, here at the Cape high court, when the judgement was read

Devi
What was that moment like?
Makoma
I couldn't believe what I was hearing from each and every point the ruling was in our favour

Up sound Liz
Victory to the people!
Liz
It was like a powerful moment of yes justice has been done


Devi
Has it registered to you that you played a fundamental role in changing the future of SA
Makoma
All of us do that every day
Devi
No, no, no all of us don't do that every day
Makoma
I am raised in a big family and I stay in a township and you don't just take credit as a person, its all of us who did that!

Commentary fourteen
But their victory has not gone unnoticed. Recently they each received a call. Both brushed it off.

Makoma
I got a WhatsApp message asking me if I know the Goldman prize, and I was busy I was …then I just disregarded this WhatsApp message

Liz
I got this phone call, I thought it's a scam, just play along

LINK
But it wasn't scam, Liz and Makoma had just been told they had won the most prestigious environmental award on the planet- The Goldman Prize - also known as the Green Nobel.

Liz
I don't see myself as the type of person who gets those kind of awards I just do my job
Devi
Did you realise how big this was?
Makoma
I went back - I only checked the website in January
Devi
To have a look?
Makoma
Ya I didn't bother the whole time
Devi
Makoma maybe you are crazy the laugh
Devi
you get told you getting this massive award but you only check it in January
Makoma
What I am doing… I am driven by passion. I am not doing what I do for someone to recognize me

Commentary Fifteen
In January at Davos, Cyril Ramaphosa told reporters that the government currently can't afford to build new nuclear reactors. Earlier this week Liz and Makoma graciously received their awards in San Francisco

Liz
When you look at the players involved, it was clear that there were strands of crookery woven through it and I think at the end what we did was maybe pull out the knot and things unraveled, but it's still possible for them to knit themselves together so we have to remain vigilant

THE END 10 30


PROMO ONE 10 seconds
Two determined South African women took the state to court to stop the new nuclear deal and against the odds they won. This week they received the international Goldman Prize

PROMO TWO 15 seconds
As the government steamrolled ahead with its new nuclear plans. Two South African women refused to accept it was a done deal
Liz
it was a case of saying we are never going to give up. We can't just let bullies get away with it. GOOD MUST TRIUMPH!

PROMO THREE
Two South Africans have just won the most prestigous environmental award in the world.

Makoma
I got a WhatsApp message asking me if I know the Goldman prize, and I was busy I was …then I just disregarded this WhatsApp message
Liz
I got this phone call, I thought it's a scam

LONG PROMO

The trillion-rand nuclear deal pushed by former President Zuma almost succeeded until these two women stepped onto the frontlines.

Liz: for me the biggest thing was that if something goes wrong the Russians would walk away, so on what basis are you giving them any incentive to do a good job?

Makoma Lekalakala
That is what our government had signed with Russia - actually putting the lives of SA at risk Devi
Is that normal? I build it, if it doesn't work out, sorry for you
Makoma
That tells us these are corrupt deals - if there are corrupt deals there will be disregard for environment and disregard for people

Liz It was like a powerful moment of yes justice has been done Devi Has it registered to you that you played a fundamental role in changing the future of SA Makoma All of us do that every day Devi No, no, no all of us don't do that every day Makoma I am raised in a big family and I stay in a township and you don't just take credit as a person, its all of us who did that! Commentary fourteen But their victory has not gone unnoticed. Recently they each received a call. Both brushed it off. Makoma I got a WhatsApp message asking me if I know the Goldman prize, and I was busy I was …then I just disregarded this WhatsApp message Liz I got this phone call, I thought it's a scam, just play along LINK But it wasn't scam, Liz and Makoma had just been told they had won the most prestigious environmental award on the planet- The Goldman Prize - also known as the Green Nobel. Liz I don't see myself as the type of person who gets those kind of awards I just do my job Devi Did you realise how big this was? Makoma I went back - I only checked the website in January Devi To have a look? Makoma Ya I didn't bother the whole time Devi Makoma maybe you are crazy the laugh Devi you get told you getting this massive award but you only check it in January Makoma What I am doing… I am driven by passion. I am not doing what I do for someone to recognize me Commentary Fifteen In January at Davos, Cyril Ramaphosa told reporters that the government currently can't afford to build new nuclear reactors. Earlier this week Liz and Makoma graciously received their awards in San Francisco Liz When you look at the players involved, it was clear that there were strands of crookery woven through it and I think at the end what we did was maybe pull out the knot and things unraveled, but it's still possible for them to knit themselves together so we have to remain vigilant THE END 10 30 PROMO ONE 10 seconds Two determined South African women took the state to court to stop the new nuclear deal and against the odds they won. This week they received the international Goldman Prize PROMO TWO 15 seconds As the government steamrolled ahead with its new nuclear plans. Two South African women refused to accept it was a done deal Liz it was a case of saying we are never going to give up. We can't just let bullies get away with it. GOOD MUST TRIUMPH! PROMO THREE Two South Africans have just won the most prestigous environmental award in the world. Makoma I got a WhatsApp message asking me if I know the Goldman prize, and I was busy I was …then I just disregarded this WhatsApp message Liz I got this phone call, I thought it's a scam LONG PROMO The trillion-rand nuclear deal pushed by former President Zuma almost succeeded until these two women stepped onto the frontlines. Liz: for me the biggest thing was that if something goes wrong the Russians would walk away, so on what basis are you giving them any incentive to do a good job? Makoma Lekalakala That is what our government had signed with Russia - actually putting the lives of SA at risk Devi Is that normal? I build it, if it doesn't work out, sorry for you Makoma That tells us these are corrupt deals - if there are corrupt deals there will be disregard for environment and disregard for people

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Two South African Nuclear activists took on the state with limited resources and one a resounding victory that could change the course of our history
metadata.Unique Selling Point: International recognition for two nuclear activists
metadata.Summary: When South Africa's Joemat Peterson signed a nuclear deal with Russia for 9600 MW of power in a secret deal that could later bankrupt the country, two tiny underfunded NGO's decided to take on the fight. This month they will receive international recognition from the worlds most prestigious environmental prize. Carte goes back to look at how this David and Goliath battle was fought and won
metadata.Further information: In its papers, Earthlife Africa Jhb and SAFCEI maintained that the minister has failed to put the necessary processes in place to ensure that the nuclear procurement deal is conducted lawfully and meets the requirements of the constitution for a fair, equitable, transparent, competitive and costs effective process: "Notwithstanding the vast sums of money to be committed, and the potentially long-term effect on the economy and for consumers of electricity and present and future generations of South Africans, the decision to proceed with procuring these nuclear power plants (the so called nuclear fleet), and to have concluded such procurement in the next few months, has occurred without any of the necessary statutory and constitutional decisions having been lawfully taken"Senior Programme Officer at Earthlife Africa Jhb. Makoma Lekalakala states: "Government's ongoing efforts to procure 9600 MW of nuclear energy behind closed doors and without taking the public into its confidence marks a critical point in the post 1994 political landscape. Civil society's attempts to obtain information on and answers to serious public interest questions regarding the potential negative impacts (such as impacts on electricity prices) of the procurement deal of the century have been frustrated and blocked at every turn. Lekalakala explains that this court case is not about the fact that nuclear energy is environmentally destructive and a false solution to the current electricity crisis, but is about lawful, constitutional, open and responsive governance. In a context of ongoing secrecy by government, the publics' right to participate in decisions that have far- reaching implications for both current and future generations of South Africans needs to be respected and protected . "We are concerned citizens standing up against the unlawful and unconstitutional exercise of power by government, and in the public interest are going to court in an effort to protect our constitutional rights". At a board meeting in October 2014, SAFCEI elected to seek legal counsel to investigate the nuclear contracts which South Africa had signed. Faith communities are gravely concerned at the government's continued support for nuclear energy despite a lack of evidence that South Africa can afford it. SAFCEI believes that this new nuclear power poses unacceptable environmental, social and economic risks to the people of South Africa and believes that concentrated focus on renewable energy is the key to alleviating poverty and addressing the developmental needs of the country. "Ethical governance has to be the cornerstone of true democracy", stated Liziwe McDaid, spokesperson for SAFCEI, "this new democracy must be protected from people in positions of power who act without regard to proper process, without accountability and risk bankrupting the country". McDaid added that: "Faith demands courage. As people of faith, we are concerned about the direction in which we are currently being led by our leadership. We request transparency, honesty and openness around the decisions being made for our future." The Russian nuclear agreement contains specific clauses that could have potentially devastating consequences for South Africa. These include that South Africa will be liable for any environmental including radioactive accidents and any resultant economic consequences, while Russia will not have any liability. It also states that South Africa cannot procure nuclear services from any other entity without the consentof Russia. SAFCEI board member and Buddist Ani Tsondru comments that: "In effect, this could result in massive economic and social impacts for South Africans. We will be in debt to the Russians nuclearcorporation, and potentially suffering from a dual burden of insufficient funds to build hosptials, houses and schools, while having to foot the bill for environmental clean-up costs if there is an accident. This is a gross injustice to the people of South Africa and must be stopped". The court application therefore seeks to set aside the framework agreements
